Not necessarily. Satellite data show about 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023 on this 58.1 ha property (about 1.2% of its area). Later years of data and a 2020 forest reference both support that the loss is real.

However, the evidence doesn't show that forest was cleared. The 2021 national forest map classifies most of the affected area as planted eucalyptus (0.4 ha), with the rest (0.3 ha) outside mapped forest and none as native forest. The loss data count any stand replacement, so this could be a plantation harvest rather than deforestation.

The evidence also can't tell us the cause (harvest, fire, storm, clearing), whether it was legal, who was responsible, or any regulatory compliance status. A further 0.4 ha of smaller-patch loss was detected but isn't counted as an event.
